steps.note: an eight second screen recording open as one clip, playing at the speed it was recorded. The panel has a Speed section for it even though nothing has been cut, because an uncut recording is one piece and one piece can be sped up

THE FIRST TEST: one click in the panel and the clip plays at four times. The bar on the timeline is a quarter of the room it took, the ruler and the transport count to two seconds rather than eight, and the piece is badged 4x. The panel says the two numbers a person would check it by, what it did about frames, and that the sound has stopped

steps.reads: One frame in every 4 is shown. The rest are skipped, never blended together.

steps.note: THE SECOND TEST, and the question everybody gets wrong: the sound. At four times it is SILENT, and the panel says so in a whole sentence in warning colour rather than dropping it quietly. Inside the band, half speed to double, it plays with the picture and is pitched by it

steps.reads: Silent. Past 2x the sound is a squeal rather than a voice, so this stretch plays with none.

steps.comment: What plays is what EXPORTS, timed rather than eyeballed: the file is written and read back, and it runs for two seconds rather than eight. The sound decision reaches it too, so a stretch the app plays silent comes out of the writer with no sound track rather than with a squeal.
steps.name: speed-at-four-times

steps.reads: Sound plays with the picture, so it is higher than you recorded it.

steps.note: back inside the band at double speed, and the sound is back, pitched up with the picture. The warning colour is gone and the sentence says which way it moved

steps.comment: ...and the other half of the same claim: back inside the band the file is four seconds and DOES carry its sound.
steps.name: speed-at-double

steps.note: THE THIRD TEST: the other direction. A quarter speed makes the clip four times longer on the timeline, and the panel is honest about what it did with frames: each recorded frame is held, nothing is invented in between. That is the sentence that stops somebody expecting the smoothing this does not do

steps.reads: Each frame of the recording is held for 4 of the frames on screen. Nothing is made up in between them.

steps.note: back to normal and cut twice, so the take is three pieces on one row with the middle one picked. The panel is now talking about that piece rather than about the whole clip

THE FOURTH TEST, and the job this feature was asked for: ONE piece of the clip at thirty times while the pieces either side of it stay as they were. A dead stretch collapses to almost nothing, everything after it slides back, and the pieces before it never moved. That is speed changing ACROSS a clip, and it is the clip's own pieces doing it rather than a second model laid over the top

THE FIFTH TEST: a held frame is not a speed, and the panel says that rather than showing a number it does not have. It says how long the frame is on screen for and why it is silent, and it points at the gesture that does change it, which is dragging its ends on the timeline

steps.reads: A held frame, not a speed.

steps.note: THE SIXTH TEST: two presses of Command Z and the piece is back at the speed it was recorded. A retime is one history step like every other edit in the app, not a mode you have to leave
